
Evaluated 8 Grok social signals and 18 arXiv RSS signals. Most Grok signals lack verifiable URLs or are fabricated (unresolvable tweet IDs, non-existent blog posts). From arXiv, two papers stand out: one on a structured critic-actor loop for agentic reasoning (directly relevant to iterative refinement and evaluation loops) and one on interpretability of agentic tool use (relevant to observability and tool-use design). The GraphDC divide-and-conquer multi-agent paper and the LLM agent memory survey are also relevant but weaker on production/empirical grounding criteria.

## Suggestions

- [SCALAR: Structured Critic–Actor Loop for Agentic Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06772) — Proposes a structured critic-actor loop architecture for agentic reasoning, directly instantiating iterative refinement and evaluation loop design patterns with empirical grounding in a physics reasoning domain.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)

- [Beyond the Black Box: Interpretability of Agentic AI Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06890) — Examines interpretability and observability of tool-use decisions in agentic AI systems, providing principled analysis of how agents select and sequence tools across the execution lifecycle.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)
